Closes the listening socket; run when a TcpListener is dropped.

TcpStream struct

A TCP connection: a stream of bytes each way.

The bytes on the wire are exactly those written, in order, with no framing or encoding added, and a read gives whatever part of them has arrived. Calls block until they complete or the stream's timeout passes (set_read_timeout_ms, set_write_timeout_ms). Dropping the stream closes it; the connection closes when the last stream on it (try_clone) is dropped. Formatted text is sent with TcpStream::printf(s, format, …), as File::printf writes to a file.

TcpStream::connect fn

Connects to a, waiting as long as the system does.

Err(Refused) when nothing listens there, Err(TimedOut), Err(Unreachable). connect_timeout bounds the wait.

TcpStream::connect_timeout fn

Connects to a, waiting at most ms milliseconds.

Err(TimedOut) when the time passes first; an ms of 0 is taken as 1. Other errors as connect's.

TcpStream::peer_addr fn

The address of the other end of the connection.

TcpStream::local_addr fn

The local address of the connection.

TcpStream::set_read_timeout_ms fn

Sets how long a read waits for data, in milliseconds; 0 waits for ever.

A read, read_exact or read_line that waits longer gives Err(TimedOut), and the stream stays usable.

TcpStream::set_write_timeout_ms fn

Sets how long a write may wait to go on, in milliseconds; 0 waits for ever.

A write that cannot go on for that long gives Err(TimedOut), and the stream stays usable.

TcpStream::set_nodelay fn

Sets whether small writes are sent at once (true) or gathered for a moment into fewer packets.

Gathering (false) is the default.

TcpStream::read fn

Appends up to max bytes of what has arrived to buf, and gives how many.

Waits until at least one byte has arrived, and reads at most a MiB in one call. With max > 0 it gives 0 exactly when the peer has closed its sending side.

TcpStream::read_exact fn

Appends exactly n bytes to buf, reading until they have all arrived.

Err(Closed) when the peer closes first; what arrived before that stays in buf.

TcpStream::read_line fn

The next line from the connection, without its \n (nor a \r before it).

Ok(None) when the peer has closed its side; Err(NotUtf8(e)) for a line that is not UTF-8. Reads as File::read_line does.

TcpStream::write fn

Sends all of data.

Err(Closed) or Err(Reset) when the peer has gone; Err(TimedOut) after the write timeout.

TcpStream::write_text fn

Sends the bytes of text, as write does.

TcpStream::shutdown_write fn

Closes the sending side of the connection; this side can still read.

The peer reads the end (0) after what was sent. Through any stream of a try_cloned pair it ends sending for all of them.

TcpStream::drop fn

Closes this stream, and the connection when no other stream (try_clone) is on it.

Run when a TcpStream is dropped.

TcpStream::set_keepalive fn

Turns TCP keepalive on or off for the connection.

With it on, the system probes an idle connection by its own schedule (after a couple of hours, by default), so a peer or a path that has silently gone makes a later read fail rather than wait for ever.

TcpStream::try_clone fn

A second TcpStream on the same connection, for reading in one thread while another writes.

Each thread takes its own stream by move. Bytes read through one are not seen by the other, and each has its own timeouts; shutdown_write through either ends sending for both, and the connection closes when the last of them is dropped.

TcpStream::printf built in fn

Writes the formatted text to the connected stream *s, as File::printf does to a file; the whole text is written or the Err says why ([Stream-Write]). A line protocol's reply in one call: TcpStream::printf(&mut c, "%d %s\r\n", code, text)?.

UdpSocket struct

A UDP socket: it sends and receives datagrams of up to about 64 KiB, each delivered whole or not at all.

The network may lose, duplicate or reorder datagrams; on loopback it does not. Dropping the socket closes it.

UdpSocket::bind fn

Opens a UDP socket bound to a; port 0 asks the system for a free port.

Errors as TcpListener::bind's.

UdpSocket::try_clone fn

A second handle on the same socket, as TcpStream::try_clone gives one.

A thread can wait for datagrams on one handle while others send on another.

UdpSocket::local_addr fn

The address the socket is bound to, with the port the system chose for port 0.

UdpSocket::set_read_timeout_ms fn

Sets how long recv_from and recv wait for a datagram, in milliseconds; 0 waits for ever.

After the timeout they give Err(TimedOut), and the socket stays usable.

UdpSocket::send_to fn

Sends data as one datagram to to, and gives the number of bytes sent.

UdpSocket::recv_from fn

Waits for the next datagram and gives its first max bytes and its sender.

The rest of a datagram longer than max is lost. Err(TimedOut) after the read timeout.

UdpSocket::drop fn

Closes the socket; run when a UdpSocket is dropped.

UdpSocket::connect fn

Fixes the peer that send sends to and recv receives from.

A datagram from any other address is then dropped. send_to and recv_from still work.

UdpSocket::send fn

Sends data as one datagram to the connected peer, and gives the number of bytes sent.

Err(Failed) on a socket that is not connected (connect).

UdpSocket::recv fn

Waits for the next datagram from the connected peer and gives its first max bytes.

The rest of a longer datagram is lost. Err(Failed) on a socket that is not connected (connect).

Datagram struct

A datagram received: its bytes (data) and its sender (from).

resolve fn

The socket addresses host names, each with port, through the system's resolver.

The resolver reads its hosts file, then DNS, and the addresses come in its order; "localhost" resolves without a network. Err(UnknownHost) when the name resolves to nothing or cannot be resolved. The call blocks until the resolver answers.

std::crypto::digest impl/std/crypto/digest.cb

Sha256 struct

A SHA-256 computation in progress (FIPS 180-4).

Make one with Sha256::new, give it the message with Sha256::update as the message arrives, and take the 32-byte digest with Sha256::finish; the digest is the same however the message is cut. A Sha256 is a plain value, so a copy continues on its own: copy one to hash two continuations of one prefix.

Not independently audited: std::crypto is implemented to the standards its documentation names, tested against their vectors and against OpenSSL, and fuzzed continuously, but it has not been independently audited.

Sha256::new fn

A SHA-256 computation that has been given nothing yet.

Sha256::update fn

Adds data to the message being hashed.

Call it as often as the message arrives; the pieces are hashed as their concatenation.

Sha256::finish fn

The 32-byte SHA-256 digest of everything given to s.

s is consumed; copy it first to go on hashing.

Sha512 struct

A SHA-512 computation in progress (FIPS 180-4).

Used as Sha256 is: Sha512::new, Sha512::update as often as needed, then Sha512::finish for the 64-byte digest. A plain value: a copy continues on its own.

Sha512::new fn

A SHA-512 computation that has been given nothing yet.

Sha512::update fn

Adds data to the message being hashed.

Sha512::finish fn

The 64-byte SHA-512 digest of everything given to s.

Sha384 struct

A SHA-384 computation in progress (FIPS 180-4).

SHA-512 with its own initial values and the digest cut to 48 bytes; used as Sha256 is. A plain value: a copy continues on its own.

Sha384::new fn

A SHA-384 computation that has been given nothing yet.

Sha384::update fn

Adds data to the message being hashed.

Sha384::finish fn

The 48-byte SHA-384 digest of everything given to s.

Sha1 struct

A SHA-1 computation in progress (FIPS 180-4), for legacy protocols only.

Used as Sha256 is, with a 20-byte digest. It is here for what older protocols still require (HMAC-SHA-1 in RFC 6238's TOTP, git's object names, old signatures to check), never for a new signature or anything whose collision resistance matters: SHA-1 collisions have been made.

Sha1::new fn

A SHA-1 computation that has been given nothing yet.

Sha1::update fn

Adds data to the message being hashed.

Sha1::finish fn

The 20-byte SHA-1 digest of everything given to s.

HashKind enum

A hash chosen at run time: SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512.

  • Sha1: SHA-1, a 20-byte digest and a 64-byte block; legacy only, as Sha1 says.
  • Sha2_256: SHA-256, a 32-byte digest and a 64-byte block.
  • Sha2_384: SHA-384, a 48-byte digest and a 128-byte block.
  • Sha2_512: SHA-512, a 64-byte digest and a 128-byte block.

It names the hash in hash, Hasher, Hmac, hmac, pbkdf2, the HKDF _with forms, the RSA signature functions and SignatureScheme.

Hasher struct

A hash computation whose HashKind is chosen at run time.

Used as Sha256 is: Hasher::new(kind), Hasher::update as often as needed, then Hasher::finish, which gives hash(kind, d) of the concatenation d of everything given. A plain value: a copy continues on its own.

Hasher::new fn

A computation of the hash kind that has been given nothing yet.

Hasher::update fn

Adds data to the message being hashed.

Hasher::finish fn

The digest of everything given to h: 20, 32, 48 or 64 bytes.

As long as the digest of its kind: SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512.

Blake2b struct

A BLAKE2b computation in progress (RFC 7693), plain or keyed.

Make one with Blake2b::new or Blake2b::new_keyed, give it the message with Blake2b::update, and take the digest with Blake2b::finish. The digest's length, 1 to 64 bytes, is chosen when it is made. A plain value: a copy continues on its own.

Blake2b::new_keyed fn

A keyed BLAKE2b computation (RFC 7693 §2.1) with a digest of out_len bytes.

key is up to 64 bytes; an empty key gives the plain hash. Faults (crypto_length) when out_len is 0 or above 64, or key is longer than 64 bytes.

Blake2b::new fn

A plain BLAKE2b computation with a digest of out_len bytes.

The same as Blake2b::new_keyed with an empty key. Faults (crypto_length) when out_len is 0 or above 64.

Blake2b::update fn

Adds data to the message being hashed.

Blake2b::finish fn

The digest of everything given to s, of the length chosen when it was made.

sha256 fn

The SHA-256 digest of data, 32 bytes.

The same as Sha256::new, one Sha256::update and Sha256::finish. to_hex prints it.

sha512 fn

The SHA-512 digest of data, 64 bytes.

sha384 fn

The SHA-384 digest of data, 48 bytes.

sha1 fn

The SHA-1 digest of data, 20 bytes; legacy, as Sha1 says.

hash fn

The digest of data by the hash kind: 20, 32, 48 or 64 bytes.

sha1, sha256, sha384 or sha512 of data, as a Vec<u8>.

blake2b fn

The BLAKE2b digest of data, out_len bytes long (64 for BLAKE2b-512).

Faults (crypto_length) when out_len is 0 or above 64.

crc32 fn

The CRC-32 checksum of data, as zlib, PNG, gzip and Ethernet compute it.

CRC-32/IEEE: polynomial 0x04C11DB7 (reflected 0xEDB88320), initial value and final exclusive or 0xFFFFFFFF, input and output reflected; computed bit by bit.

It is not cryptographic: it detects accidental corruption, and anyone can make data with any CRC they choose. To detect tampering, use a hash or a MAC.

digest_eq fn

Whether a and b have the same length and the same bytes, in a time that depends on the lengths alone.

Every byte is compared, however early they differ, so a sender guessing a MAC learns nothing from how long the check took. A program that checks a MAC or a digest it received compares with this, never ==. Slices of different lengths are false.

std::crypto::kdf impl/std/crypto/kdf.cb

HmacSha256 struct

An HMAC-SHA-256 computation in progress (RFC 2104).

Make one with HmacSha256::new(key), give it the message with HmacSha256::update, and take the 32-byte MAC with HmacSha256::finish. A plain value: a copy of a keyed HmacSha256 continues on its own, so one key setup serves many messages.

HmacSha256::new fn

An HMAC-SHA-256 computation under key that has been given no message yet.

key may be of any length: one longer than 64 bytes is replaced by its SHA-256 digest, then the key is padded with zero bytes to 64.

HmacSha256::update fn

Adds data to the message being authenticated.

HmacSha256::finish fn

The 32-byte MAC of everything given to m.

Hmac struct

An HMAC computation in progress (RFC 2104) over a hash chosen at run time.

Used as HmacSha256 is: Hmac::new(kind, key), Hmac::update, then Hmac::finish. A plain value: a copy of a keyed Hmac continues on its own, which is how pbkdf2 reuses one key setup for every iteration.

Hmac::new fn

An HMAC computation over the hash kind under key that has been given no message yet.

A key longer than the hash's block (64 bytes for SHA-1 and SHA-256, 128 for SHA-384 and SHA-512) is replaced by its digest, then padded with zero bytes to the block.

Hmac::update fn

Adds data to the message being authenticated.

Hmac::finish fn

The MAC of everything given to m, as long as its hash's digest.

hmac_sha256 fn

The HMAC-SHA-256 of data under key (RFC 2104), 32 bytes.

Check a MAC that arrived with digest_eq, never ==.

hkdf_extract fn

The 32-byte HKDF-SHA-256 pseudorandom key of ikm under salt (RFC 5869).

HMAC-SHA-256 of ikm with salt as the key; an empty salt stands for 32 zero bytes.

hkdf_expand fn

The first len bytes of HKDF-SHA-256 output keying material from prk and info (RFC 5869).

Block i is HMAC-SHA-256(prk, block i-1 ‖ info ‖ i), block 0 being empty and i one byte counted from 1. Faults (hkdf_length) when len is above 8160 (255 blocks).

hkdf_sha256 fn

HKDF-SHA-256 in one call: len bytes derived from ikm with salt and info.

The same as hkdf_expand of hkdf_extract(salt, ikm), info and len. Faults (hkdf_length) when len is above 8160.

hkdf_expand_label fn

TLS 1.3's HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 §7.1): len bytes from secret, label and context.

hkdf_expand of secret with the info len in two bytes ‖ the length of "tls13 " ‖ label in one byte ‖ "tls13 " ‖ label ‖ the length of context in one byte ‖ context. The key schedules of TLS 1.3, QUIC and DTLS 1.3 are built from it.

Faults (hkdf_length) when len is above 8160; a label longer than 249 bytes or a context longer than 255 faults (narrowing_overflow) while the info is built.

hmac fn

The HMAC of data under key over the hash kind, as long as that hash's digest.

hmac(Sha2_256, key, data) gives the same bytes as hmac_sha256(key, data).

hkdf_extract_with fn

The HKDF pseudorandom key of ikm under salt over the hash kind (RFC 5869).

As hkdf_extract, with kind's digest length in place of 32: an empty salt stands for that many zero bytes, and the key is that long.

hkdf_expand_with fn

The first len bytes of HKDF output keying material from prk and info over the hash kind.

As hkdf_expand, with HMAC over kind. Faults (hkdf_length) when len is above 255 of kind's digests.

hkdf_with fn

HKDF over the hash kind in one call: len bytes derived from ikm with salt and info.

The same as hkdf_expand_with of hkdf_extract_with(kind, salt, ikm), info and len.

hkdf_expand_label_with fn

TLS 1.3's HKDF-Expand-Label over the hash kind, as the SHA-384 cipher suites use it.

As hkdf_expand_label, with hkdf_expand_with over kind: len above 255 of kind's digests faults (hkdf_length).

pbkdf2 fn

PBKDF2 (RFC 8018 §5.2) over HMAC of kind: len bytes derived from password and salt.

Each block of the result costs iterations HMACs. It is here for the formats that still use it (SCRAM among them); to store a password, use hash_password. Faults (kdf_parameters) when iterations is 0.

argon2id fn

The Argon2id tag (RFC 9106, version 0x13) of len bytes from password and salt.

iterations passes over memory_kib kibibytes, rounded down to a multiple of 4 × parallelism, in parallelism lanes, computed one after another; no secret key and no associated data. The first two slices of the first pass address memory independently of the password and the rest depend on it, as Argon2id prescribes; that addressing is outside std::crypto's constant-time guarantee.

Faults (kdf_parameters) when iterations is 0, parallelism is 0 or above 255, memory_kib is below 8 × parallelism, salt is shorter than 8 bytes or len is below 4.

Cost: time grows with iterations × memory_kib, and memory_kib KiB are allocated. To store a password, hash_password chooses the parameters.

hash_password fn

password hashed for storage: an Argon2id PHC string with a fresh random salt.

The text $argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$S$H, S the unpadded base64 of 16 bytes of os_random_bytes and H that of argon2id(password, salt, 2, 19456, 1, 32): 19 MiB, two passes and one lane, the OWASP recommendation. verify_password and every password library read it.

Slow by design, so that guessing stays expensive: under coby it takes over half an hour.

verify_password fn

Whether password is the one the Argon2id PHC string stored was made from.

stored is a hash written by hash_password or by any Argon2id implementation ($argon2id$v=19$m=M,t=T,p=P$salt$hash); its parameters are taken from it, and the result is compared with digest_eq. false when stored does not have that shape or its parameters are outside the bounds argon2id accepts, so it never faults on them. Cost: one argon2id with the stored parameters.

std::crypto::aead impl/std/crypto/aead.cb

chacha20 fn

data exclusive-ored with the ChaCha20 keystream (RFC 8439 §2.4) for key and nonce, from block counter.

Encryption and decryption are the same operation. key is 32 bytes and nonce 12. The stream cipher alone hides the data but does not protect it from change; use chacha20_poly1305_seal for that. Constant-time: the steps taken depend on the lengths of the arguments only.

Faults (crypto_length) for another key or nonce length, or when data would need a block counter past 2^32 - 1.

poly1305 fn

The 16-byte Poly1305 tag of message under the one-time 32-byte key (RFC 8439 §2.5).

A key must never authenticate two messages; chacha20_poly1305_seal derives a fresh one for each nonce. Constant-time: the steps taken depend on the lengths of the arguments only. Faults (crypto_length) when key is not 32 bytes.

chacha20_poly1305_seal fn

Encrypts and authenticates plaintext with ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439 §2.8).

The result is the ciphertext, as long as plaintext, followed by a 16-byte tag over it and over aad, data sent in the clear but protected from change. key is 32 bytes and nonce 12; a nonce must never be used twice with one key. Constant-time: the steps taken depend on the lengths of the arguments only. Faults (crypto_length) for another key or nonce length.

chacha20_poly1305_open fn

Checks and decrypts what chacha20_poly1305_seal gave, under the same key, nonce and aad.

Some(plaintext) when the tag matches; None when anything was changed, the key, nonce or aad differ, or sealed is shorter than the 16-byte tag. The tag is checked with digest_eq, and nothing of a refused message is returned. Faults (crypto_length) for a key that is not 32 bytes or a nonce that is not 12.

aes_encrypt_block fn

One 16-byte block encrypted with AES (FIPS 197) under key.

key is 16, 24 or 32 bytes, for AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256. The bare block cipher, for building other modes; to encrypt data, use aes_gcm_seal. Constant-time: the steps taken depend on the lengths of the arguments only. Faults (crypto_length) for another key length.

aes_gcm_seal fn

Encrypts and authenticates plaintext with AES-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D) under key and nonce.

The result is the ciphertext, as long as plaintext, followed by a 16-byte tag over it and over aad. key is 16, 24 or 32 bytes (AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256) and nonce 12; a nonce must never be used twice with one key. Constant-time: the steps taken depend on the lengths of the arguments only. Faults (crypto_length) for another key or nonce length.

aes_gcm_open fn

Checks and decrypts what aes_gcm_seal gave, under the same key, nonce and aad.

Some(plaintext) when the tag matches; None when anything was changed, the key, nonce or aad differ, or sealed is shorter than the 16-byte tag. The tag is checked with digest_eq, and nothing of a refused message is returned. Faults (crypto_length) for a key that is not 16, 24 or 32 bytes or a nonce that is not 12.

std::crypto::pk impl/std/crypto/pk.cb

RsaPublicKey struct

An RSA public key: the modulus n and the public exponent e.

EcCurve enum

An elliptic curve for ECDH and ECDSA.

  • P256: NIST P-256 (secp256r1): private keys and shared secrets of 32 bytes, public keys of 65.
  • P384: NIST P-384 (secp384r1): private keys and shared secrets of 48 bytes, public keys of 97.

RsaPrivateKey struct

An RSA private key: the modulus n, the public exponent e, the private exponent d and the primes p and q.

Made by RsaPrivateKey::new, rsa_generate_key or PrivateKey::from_der; it also holds the Chinese-remainder values the private operation uses. Signing computes m^d mod n modulo p and q with a constant-time exponentiation and checks the result with e.

RsaPrivateKey::new fn

The private key with these parts, or None when they do not fit together.

They fit when p and q are odd and above 2, p·q = n, and e·d ≡ 1 modulo p - 1 and modulo q - 1.

RsaPrivateKey::public_key fn

The public half of key: its modulus and public exponent.

x25519 fn

The X25519 shared secret (RFC 7748) of private_key and the other side's public_key.

Both are 32 bytes; the result is the clamped private key times the point with u-coordinate public_key on Curve25519. None when the result is all zeros, which a public key of small order gives and which must never be used as a secret (TLS 1.3 requires the check). Constant-time, the check for zero included. Faults (crypto_length) when either is not 32 bytes.

x25519_public_key fn

The X25519 public key of the 32-byte private_key: the private key times the base point u = 9.

Constant-time. Faults (crypto_length) when private_key is not 32 bytes.

x25519_private_key fn

A new X25519 private key: 32 bytes of os_random_bytes.

From the operating system's secure source, never from Rng.

rsa_verify_pkcs1v15 fn

Whether signature is key's RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 signature (RFC 8017 §8.2.2) of a message whose kind digest is digest.

digest is the hash of the message, not the message. True exactly when signature is as long as the modulus, below it, and signature^e mod n is 00 01 FF…FF 00 ‖ the DigestInfo of kind ‖ digest with at least eight FF bytes; the block is rebuilt and compared whole, so no part of it is parsed. A malformed key or signature gives false, never a fault. Not constant-time, and need not be: it uses public values only.

rsa_verify_pss fn

Whether signature is key's RSASSA-PSS signature (RFC 8017 §8.1.2) of a message whose kind digest is digest.

With MGF1 over the same hash and a salt as long as the digest, as TLS 1.3 and most X.509 use. A malformed key or signature gives false, never a fault. Not constant-time, and need not be: it uses public values only.

ecdsa_verify fn

Whether signature is an ECDSA signature (FIPS 186-4 §6.4.2) on curve by the holder of public_key of a message whose digest is digest.

public_key is an uncompressed point (0x04 ‖ x ‖ y) on the curve, and signature the strict DER SEQUENCE { r INTEGER, s INTEGER } of X.509 and TLS, with r and s in [1, n-1]. The digest's leftmost bits are used when it is longer than the curve's order. A malformed key or signature gives false, never a fault. Not constant-time, and need not be: it uses public values only.

ec_private_key fn

A new private key for curve: 32 (P-256) or 48 (P-384) bytes of os_random_bytes.

The bytes name a number in [1, n-1]; they are drawn again in the rare case they do not.

ec_public_key fn

The public key of private_key on curve: 0x04 ‖ x ‖ y of the private key times the base point.

65 bytes on P-256, 97 on P-384; None when private_key does not name a number in [1, n-1]. Constant-time. Faults (crypto_length) when private_key is not 32 bytes (P-256) or 48 (P-384).

ecdh fn

The ECDH shared secret (SEC 1 §3.3.1) of private_key and the peer's public_key on curve.

The x-coordinate of their product: 32 bytes on P-256, 48 on P-384. None when private_key does not name a number in [1, n-1], or public_key is not an uncompressed point on the curve (a point off the curve could leak the key it is multiplied by). Constant-time. Faults (crypto_length) for a private key of the wrong length.

p256_private_key fn

A new P-256 private key: ec_private_key(P256) as a 32-byte array.

p256_public_key fn

The P-256 public key of private_key, as a 65-byte array.

ec_public_key(P256, private_key), with its None and its fault.

p256_ecdh fn

The P-256 shared secret of private_key and public_key, as a 32-byte array.

ecdh(P256, private_key, public_key), with its None and its fault.

ecdsa_sign fn

The ECDSA signature (FIPS 186-4 §6.4.1) by private_key on curve of a message whose digest is digest.

The strict DER SEQUENCE { r, s } that ecdsa_verify checks, or None when private_key does not name a number in [1, n-1]. The nonce is RFC 6979's, derived from the key and the digest with HMAC-SHA-256 (P-256) or HMAC-SHA-384 (P-384), so the same message signs the same way every time and no random number can repeat. Constant-time but for one branch, on whether a candidate nonce is below n. Faults (crypto_length) for a private key of the wrong length.

ed25519_private_key fn

A new Ed25519 private key: 32 bytes of os_random_bytes.

ed25519_public_key fn

The Ed25519 public key (RFC 8032 §5.1.5) of the 32-byte private_key.

The encoding of s·B, s the clamped first half of SHA-512(private_key). Constant-time. Faults (crypto_length) when private_key is not 32 bytes.

ed25519_sign fn

The Ed25519 signature (RFC 8032 §5.1.6) of message by private_key: R ‖ S, 64 bytes.

message is signed whole, not a digest of it. The signature is the same for the same key and message every time, with no random number to repeat. Constant-time. Faults (crypto_length) when private_key is not 32 bytes.

ed25519_verify fn

Whether signature is public_key's Ed25519 signature (RFC 8032 §5.1.7) of message.

True exactly when public_key and signature are 32 and 64 bytes, the key and R (the signature's first 32 bytes) are canonical point encodings, S (the rest, little-endian) is below L, and S·B = R + k·A with k = SHA-512(R ‖ A ‖ message) mod L. Anything else, a wrong length included, is false. Not constant-time, and need not be: it uses public values only.

rsa_sign_pkcs1v15 fn

key's RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 signature (RFC 8017 §8.2.1) of a message whose kind digest is digest.

As many bytes as the modulus, and the same every time; rsa_verify_pkcs1v15 with the key's public half accepts it. Faults (crypto_length) when digest is not as long as kind's digests, or the modulus is shorter than the encoding plus 11 bytes.

rsa_sign_pss fn

key's RSASSA-PSS signature (RFC 8017 §8.1.1) of a message whose kind digest is digest.

With MGF1 over the same hash and a salt of os_random_bytes as long as the digest: a different signature every time, each accepted by rsa_verify_pss. Faults (crypto_length) when digest is not as long as kind's digests, or the modulus is too short for two digests and two bytes.

rsa_generate_key fn

A new RSA private key of bits bits, with the public exponent 65537.

n = p·q has exactly bits bits; p and q are distinct primes of bits/2 bits from os_random_bytes, found by trial division by the primes below 1000 and five rounds of Miller–Rabin with random bases (FIPS 186-4 B.3.3), with p - 1 and q - 1 prime to e. Faults (crypto_length) when bits is below 1024, above 8192 or not a multiple of 64. Slow under an interpreter, as every key generation is.

std::x509 impl/std/x509.cb

CertError enum

Why a certificate, a chain or a key was refused.

  • BadEncoding: the DER or PEM is malformed, or is not what was asked for.
  • Expired: a certificate's validity ended before the time checked.
  • NotYetValid: a certificate's validity begins after the time checked.
  • UnknownAuthority: no chain from the leaf reaches a trusted root.
  • HostMismatch: the leaf certificate is not for the host.
  • BadSignature: a certificate's signature does not verify under its issuer's key.
  • NotAuthority: an issuer is not a CA allowed to sign certificates, or its path length is exceeded.
  • UnsupportedAlgorithm: a key or signature algorithm std does not handle, or an encrypted private key.
  • UnhandledCritical: a certificate has a critical extension std does not handle.
  • WrongUsage: the leaf's extended key usage does not allow a TLS server.
  • ChainTooLong: no root was reached within 10 certificates.

CertError::text fn

A short English description of e, such as "certificate expired", for a message.

Der struct

One DER element (ITU-T X.690), as der_read reads it: its tag and where its contents lie.

  • tag: the tag byte.
  • start, end: the contents are buf[start..end] of the buffer it was read from.
  • next: where the next element begins, the same as end.

EcPublicKey struct

An elliptic-curve public key: the curve and the uncompressed point (0x04 ‖ x ‖ y).

CertKey enum

A public key, as a certificate or a SubjectPublicKeyInfo carries it.

  • RsaKey: an RSA key.
  • EcKey: a P-256 or P-384 key.
  • Ed25519Key: an Ed25519 key, 32 bytes.
  • UnsupportedKey: a key of another algorithm; a certificate with one parses, but no signature verifies under it.

CertKey::to_der fn

The DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo of key, or None for UnsupportedKey.

CertKey::from_der reads it back.

CertKey::from_der fn

The public key of the DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo der.

Err(BadEncoding) when der is not exactly one SubjectPublicKeyInfo; Err(UnsupportedAlgorithm) when its algorithm is not RSA, P-256, P-384 or Ed25519.

CertKey::from_pem fn

The public key of the first -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY----- block in text (RFC 7468).

The block's DER is read as CertKey::from_der reads it; Err(BadEncoding) when there is no such block, or its base64 does not decode.

CertKey::to_pem fn

key as a PEM PUBLIC KEY block of 64-character lines, or None for UnsupportedKey.

SignatureScheme enum

A signature algorithm with its hash, as certificates and TLS name them.

  • RsaPkcs1(h): RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 over the hash h.
  • RsaPss(h): RSASSA-PSS over h, with MGF1 over h and a salt as long as its digest.
  • Ecdsa(h): ECDSA over h.
  • Ed25519: Ed25519, over the message itself.
  • UnsupportedSignature: another algorithm; nothing verifies or signs with it.

Certificate struct

A parsed X.509 certificate (RFC 5280), v3 or older.

  • der: the whole certificate; tbs: the signed part; signature: the signature over tbs, made with scheme.
  • issuer, subject: the names' DER, compared whole.
  • common_name: the subject's last common name, empty when there is none; host matching does not consult it.
  • not_before, not_after: the validity.
  • dns_names, ip_addresses: the subject alternative names' DNS names and IP addresses.
  • is_ca, max_path_len: the basic constraints; max_path_len is -1 when there is no limit.
  • can_sign_certificates: key usage's keyCertSign, true when there is no key usage.
  • server_auth: extended key usage allows server authentication or any use, true when there is no extended key usage.
  • unhandled_critical: a critical extension other than certificate policies or name constraints was not understood, so the certificate is not usable.
  • key: the subject's public key.

Not independently audited: std::x509 is implemented to the standards its documentation names, tested against OpenSSL, and fuzzed continuously, but it has not been independently audited.

Certificate::parse fn

The certificate whose DER is der (RFC 5280 §4.1), or Err(BadEncoding).

der must be exactly one certificate, with its inner and outer signature algorithms equal. UTCTime years 50 to 99 are read as 19xx. An unknown key or signature algorithm still parses, as UnsupportedKey or UnsupportedSignature; an unknown critical extension sets unhandled_critical. An Ed25519 key or signature algorithm (OID 1.3.101.112) is Ed25519Key or Ed25519.

Certificate::matches_host fn

Whether c is for host (RFC 6125 §6.4).

An IP address literal is compared with the certificate's IP addresses. A name is compared with its DNS names, ignoring ASCII case and one final dot on host; a leading *. in a DNS name stands for exactly one whole label, and only where at least two labels follow it (so *.com matches nothing). The common name is not consulted.

TrustStore struct

The root certificates a chain may end at, for verify_chain.

roots may be read and changed directly; TrustStore::system reads the operating system's.

TrustStore::new fn

A store with no roots.

TrustStore::add fn

Adds root to the roots of t.

TrustStore::from_pem_file fn

The roots in the PEM file at path, such as /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt.

Its certificates are read as certificates_from_pem reads them. Err with the FileError when the file cannot be read.

TrustStore::system fn

The operating system's roots, from the first of the usual bundle files that holds a certificate.

The files tried, in order: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt (Debian, Ubuntu), /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt (Fedora, RHEL), /etc/ssl/ca-bundle.pem, /etc/ssl/cert.pem (Alpine) and /usr/local/etc/openssl/cert.pem (macOS with a package manager's OpenSSL). Err(NotFound) where none does, as on Windows: a program there passes a bundle to TrustStore::from_pem_file.

EcPrivateKey struct

An elliptic-curve private key: the curve and the scalar, 32 bytes for P-256 or 48 for P-384.

PrivateKey enum

A private key of one of the algorithms std signs with.

  • RsaPrivate: an RSA key.
  • EcPrivate: a P-256 or P-384 key.
  • Ed25519Private: an Ed25519 key, its 32-byte private key (the seed).

PrivateKey::public_key fn

The public key that matches key.

An EC key whose scalar does not name a number in [1, n-1], which PrivateKey::from_der never gives, gets an empty point; a scalar of the wrong length faults (crypto_length).

PrivateKey::from_der fn

The private key of the DER der: a PKCS #8 PrivateKeyInfo (RFC 5958), PKCS #1 RSAPrivateKey or SEC 1 ECPrivateKey.

The three are told apart by their first fields; a SEC 1 key's curve comes from its own parameters. The numbers are checked as RsaPrivateKey::new and ec_public_key check them. Err(BadEncoding) when der is none of these or its numbers do not fit together; Err(UnsupportedAlgorithm) for an algorithm or curve std does not sign with.

PrivateKey::to_der fn

key as DER PKCS #8 (version 0), which PrivateKey::from_der reads back.

An RSA key with its Chinese-remainder values, an EC key with its public key, an Ed25519 key as its seed.

PrivateKey::from_pem fn

The private key of a PRIVATE KEY, RSA PRIVATE KEY or EC PRIVATE KEY block in text.

The block's DER is read as PrivateKey::from_der reads it. The labels are looked for in that order, so a PRIVATE KEY block is taken even when a block of the other kinds comes before it. An ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY block alone is Err(UnsupportedAlgorithm); no block, or base64 that does not decode, is Err(BadEncoding).

PrivateKey::to_pem fn

key as a PEM PRIVATE KEY block (PKCS #8) of 64-character lines.

der_read fn

The DER element at at in buf, or None when it is not well-formed.

Well-formed means a single-byte tag, the shortest length form, at most four length bytes, no indefinite length, and contents inside buf. Read an element's first child by calling it again at start, and the element after it at next.

certificates_from_pem fn

Every certificate in the PEM text, in order: its -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- blocks (RFC 7468).

Text between blocks is ignored. A block whose base64 does not decode, that holds a byte that is not ASCII, or that is not a certificate, is skipped.

verify_signature fn

Whether signature over message verifies under key with scheme.

The RSA and ECDSA schemes hash message with the scheme's hash first; Ed25519 checks message itself. A key of another kind than the scheme, UnsupportedKey, UnsupportedSignature or a malformed signature gives false. Not constant-time, and need not be: it uses public values only.

verify_chain fn

Verifies a TLS server's certificate chain from leaf to one of roots, for host at the time now.

Ok(()) when the leaf matches host (Certificate::matches_host), may serve TLS, is in date and usable, and a chain of at most 10 certificates exists (RFC 5280 §6, as a client needs it) in which:

  • each certificate is signed by the next, found by issuer name and signature among intermediates, in any order, or among the roots;
  • every issuer is a CA allowed to sign certificates, in date, and within its path length;
  • the last is one of the roots.

Otherwise Err of the first reason met: HostMismatch, then WrongUsage, then NotYetValid, Expired or UnhandledCritical for the leaf, then the chain's (UnknownAuthority, BadSignature, NotAuthority, NotYetValid, Expired, UnhandledCritical or ChainTooLong).

sign fn

key's signature of message under scheme, which verify_signature accepts with the matching public key.

The RSA PKCS #1 v1.5, RSA-PSS and ECDSA schemes sign the scheme's hash of message; Ed25519 signs message whole. None when key is not of the scheme's kind, the scheme is UnsupportedSignature, or an EC key's scalar is not in [1, n-1]. An RSA modulus too short for the scheme's hash faults (crypto_length).

std::tls impl/std/tls.cb

TlsError enum

Why a TLS connection failed.

  • TlsNetFailure(e): the socket failed as e says; also a line read_line read that is not UTF-8 (NotUtf8), and a read_exact cut short (Closed).
  • CertRejected(e): the server's certificate chain did not verify, as e says.
  • HandshakeFailed: a negotiation this side cannot complete.
  • ProtocolError: the peer sent a malformed message.
  • PeerAlert(code): the peer sent an alert with this description code (40 handshake_failure, 70 protocol_version, and so on).
  • RecordRejected: a record did not authenticate.

TlsError::text fn

A one-line description of the error, for messages; the common alert codes are named.

TlsStream struct

A TLS 1.3 connection over a TcpStream, as a client (client, connect) or as a server (server).

It speaks the cipher suites TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, the key exchanges X25519, P-256 and P-384, and ECDSA, RSA-PSS and Ed25519 signatures. No TLS 1.2, no session resumption, no early data, no client certificates. Dropping the stream closes the connection without close_notify; close sends it first.

Implemented to RFC 8446, tested against its vectors and against OpenSSL on loopback, and fuzzed continuously; not independently audited.

TlsStream::peer_certificate fn

The peer's certificate that the handshake verified: on a client's stream, the server's leaf.

None on a server's stream, since clients send none. A program that pins a key or a certificate compares it here.

TlsStream::peer_addr fn

The address of the other end of the connection.

TlsStream::local_addr fn

The local address of the connection.

TlsStream::client fn

Performs the TLS 1.3 handshake as a client over the connected tcp, and gives the stream.

server_name is a DNS name, sent as SNI and checked against the certificate, or an IP address literal, checked against its IP addresses. The server's chain is verified against roots at the current time. The timeouts set on tcp apply to every read and write. Err(CertRejected(e)) for a chain that does not verify, Err(HandshakeFailed) for a negotiation this client cannot complete, Err(PeerAlert(code)) when the server refuses.

TlsStream::connect fn

Connects to addr with TcpStream::connect and performs the handshake as client does.

A failure to connect is Err(TlsNetFailure(e)). For a bounded wait, connect with TcpStream::connect_timeout and call client.

TlsStream::write fn

Sends all of data, encrypted, in records of at most 16 KiB.

TlsStream::write_text fn

Sends the bytes of text, as write does.

TlsStream::read fn

Appends up to max bytes of the peer's data to buf, waiting for some, and gives how many.

0 when the peer has closed the connection with close_notify (or when max is 0). Key updates and session tickets the peer sends are handled on the way. Err(RecordRejected) for a record that does not authenticate, Err(PeerAlert(code)) for an alert.

TlsStream::read_exact fn

Appends exactly n bytes of the peer's data to buf, reading until they have all arrived.

Err(TlsNetFailure(Closed)) when the peer closes first; what arrived before that stays in buf.

TlsStream::read_line fn

The next line the peer sent, without its \n (nor a \r before it).

Ok(None) when the peer has closed (close_notify) before any byte; a last line without \n is given as it is. Err(TlsNetFailure(NotUtf8(e))) for a line that is not UTF-8.

TlsStream::close fn

Sends close_notify, telling the peer that no more data follows.

The peer may still send what it had in flight, and read still reads it. Dropping a TlsStream without close just closes the connection.

TlsStream::server fn

Performs the TLS 1.3 handshake as a server over the accepted tcp, and gives the stream.

key is the server's private key and chain its certificate first, then its issuers up to, but not including, the root. The suite and the group are chosen in the client's order of preference. A client that does not speak TLS 1.3, or offers no suite, group or signature scheme in common, is sent an alert and the result is Err(HandshakeFailed), as it is for an empty chain. The timeouts set on tcp apply to every read and write.

std::http impl/std/http.cb

HttpError enum

Why an HTTP request or connection failed.

  • HttpNetFailure(e): the network failed, as e says.
  • HttpTlsFailure(e): the TLS connection failed, as e says.
  • BadUrl: the URL is malformed (Url::parse).
  • UnsupportedScheme: the URL's scheme is neither http nor https.
  • NoRoots: an https request needed the system's trusted roots and TrustStore::system failed.
  • BadMessage: an HTTP message received is malformed.
  • TooLarge: a message's head is over 65536 bytes, or its body over the limit.
  • TooManyRedirects: a response asked for one redirect more than the client's max_redirects.
  • ConnectionClosed: the connection ended inside a message.

HttpError::text fn

A one-line description of the error, for messages.

Url struct

A parsed absolute URL, scheme://host[:port]/path?query.

  • scheme: lower-cased.
  • host: lower-cased; an IPv6 host keeps its brackets ([::1]).
  • port: the number after the host's :, or the scheme's default: 443 for https, 80 otherwise.
  • path: "/" when the text has none.
  • query: the text after ?, without it; empty when there is none.

The fragment (#…), which never reaches a server, is dropped.

Url::parse fn

Parses an absolute URL.

Err(BadUrl) for text without ://, with an empty host part, with user information (user@), or with a port that is not a number up to 65535. The scheme is not checked here: HttpClient::send gives Err(UnsupportedScheme) for one that is neither http nor https.

Url::target fn

The request target: the path, then ? and the query when the query is not empty.

Url::text fn

The URL as text again, with the port only when it is not the scheme's default.

The fragment, dropped by Url::parse, does not come back.

Url::query_pairs fn

The parameters of the URL's query, as form_decode reads them.

Param struct

One name and value of a query string or an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body.

Names compare exactly (find_param), unlike a header's.

Param::new fn

A parameter with a copy of name and of value.

Header struct

One header field: a name and a value.

Names compare without regard to ASCII case (find_header).

Header::new fn

A header with a copy of name and of value.

Request struct

An HTTP request: the method, the URL, the headers and the body.

For the client, url is absolute (https://…); for a request a server received, it is the target as sent (/path?query). A server's request has the body decoded if it came chunked.

Request::new fn

A request with method and url, no headers and an empty body.

Request::header fn

The value of the request's first header named name, ignoring ASCII case.

Response struct

An HTTP response: the status, its reason phrase, the headers and the whole body.

The client gives the body decoded if it came chunked, and decompressed if it came with Content-Encoding: gzip or deflate (that header and Content-Length are then dropped).

Response::header fn

The value of the response's first header named name, ignoring ASCII case.

Response::text fn

The body as text: a copy of its bytes, which must be UTF-8.

Err(e) when they are not.

percent_encode fn

Percent-encodes bytes as RFC 3986 does: unreserved bytes as they are, every other as %XX.

The unreserved bytes are ASCII letters and digits, -, ., _ and ~; the hex digits are upper case. A space becomes %20; form_encode writes it as +.

percent_decode fn

The bytes text percent-encodes, each %XX decoded.

None for a % not followed by two hex digits; hex digits of either case are read. A + stays a +; form_decode reads it as a space.

find_param fn

The value of the first parameter named exactly name, or None when there is none.

The comparison is case-sensitive, unlike find_header's.

form_decode fn

The parameters of a query string (without its ?) or of an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body.

The text is split into name=value pairs at & and ;, and empty pairs are skipped. A pair without = has an empty value. Each name and value is read with + as a space and then percent-decoded; one that is not UTF-8 after decoding, or holds a bad escape, is kept as given, so nothing is lost.

form_encode fn

Encodes params as a query string or form body that form_decode reads back.

The pairs are name=value, joined by &, each name and value percent-encoded with a space as +. There is no leading ?.

find_header fn

The value of the first header named name, ignoring ASCII case, or None when there is none.

reason_phrase fn

The reason phrase RFC 9110 gives a status code, such as "Not Found" for 404.

"" for a status it does not list here.

std::http::client impl/std/http/client.cb

HttpClient struct

An HTTP/1.1 client: the settings and the state it carries from request to request.

  • roots: the trusted roots https verifies servers against; None until the first https request loads the system's (TrustStore::system), or a store the program puts there.
  • timeout_ms: the timeout for connecting and for each read and write, in milliseconds.
  • max_redirects: how many redirects send follows.
  • max_body: the most bytes a response body may have, after decompression too (TooLarge beyond).
  • headers: sent with every request; a request's own header of the same name replaces one.
  • keep_alive: when set, the last connection is kept open while the server allows, and the next request to the same origin goes on it; when not (the default), each request has its own connection.

A program that makes several https requests keeps one client, so the roots are loaded once.

HttpClient::new fn

A client with the default settings.

No roots loaded yet, a 30 s timeout, up to 10 redirects, a 16 MiB body limit, keep_alive off, and the headers User-Agent and Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate.

HttpClient::send fn

Sends req and gives the final response, following redirects.

  • req.url is absolute; a scheme other than http or https is Err(UnsupportedScheme). The host's addresses are tried in turn.
  • The request carries Host, the client's headers and then the request's own (Host, Content-Length and Connection of the request are ignored), Content-Length when the body is not empty or the method is POST, PUT or PATCH, and Connection: close unless keep_alive is set.
  • Interim responses (status 1xx) are read past. A body sent with Content-Encoding: gzip or deflate arrives decoded.
  • A 301, 302 or 303 with a Location is followed by GET without the body (HEAD stays HEAD), a 307 or 308 with the method and body kept; a redirect without Location is given as it is. One redirect more than max_redirects is Err(TooManyRedirects). Once a redirect leaves the request's origin (scheme, host and port), Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie, the client's and the request's, are not sent again.
  • On a kept connection that proves closed before any of the response arrives, an idempotent request (GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE) is sent again on a fresh connection; another is Err(ConnectionClosed), since the server may have acted on it.
  • Network and TLS failures are Err(HttpNetFailure(e)) and Err(HttpTlsFailure(e)); see HttpError for the rest.

http_get fn

Sends a GET of url with a fresh HttpClient::new() and gives the response.

For https each call loads the system's roots again; a program that makes several requests keeps an HttpClient.

http_post fn

Sends a POST of body to url, with Content-Type: content_type, from a fresh default client.

As http_get, a program that makes several requests keeps an HttpClient.

std::http::server impl/std/http/server.cb

HttpServer struct

A listening HTTP/1.1 server: accept gives each client's connection.

  • max_body: the most bytes a request body may have (TooLarge beyond); 16 MiB from bind.
  • timeout_ms: the timeout for each read and write on the connections it accepts, in milliseconds; 30 s from bind.

The limits apply to every connection accepted after they are set. A server program handles each connection in a thread of its own (spawn). Dropping the server closes its listening socket.

HttpServer::bind fn

An HTTP server listening at a, with a 16 MiB body limit and a 30 s timeout per read and write.

Port 0 asks the system for a free port (local_addr names it). Errors as TcpListener::bind's.

HttpServer::bind_tls fn

An HTTPS server listening at a: each connection it accepts first completes a TLS 1.3 handshake.

key is the server's private key and chain its certificate first, then its issuers, as TlsStream::server takes them. Otherwise as bind.

HttpServer::local_addr fn

The address the server listens at, with the port the system chose for port 0.

HttpServer::accept fn

Waits for the next client and gives its connection, with the server's limits and timeouts.

For an https server the TLS handshake comes first: a client that fails it is Err(HttpTlsFailure(e)), and the server is ready for the next. A failure of the listener is Err(HttpNetFailure(e)).

HttpConnection struct

One client's connection to an HttpServer: request, then respond, repeated while it stays open.

The connection stays open for the next request when the request is HTTP/1.1 without Connection: close, or HTTP/1.0 with Connection: keep-alive. Dropping it closes the socket; close ends it cleanly first.

HttpConnection::peer_addr fn

The client's address.

HttpConnection::request fn

Reads the client's next request, or gives None when there is none to read.

  • Ok(Some(r)): r.url is the target as sent (/path?query); the body is read by Content-Length or chunked encoding, and there is none without them. When the request expects 100-continue, the HTTP/1.1 100 Continue is sent before the body is read.
  • Ok(None): the client closed before a request, or the last response ended the connection.
  • Err(BadMessage): a malformed request line, header or body, or an HTTP/1.1 request without Host; Err(TooLarge): a head over 65536 bytes or a body over max_body. The caller answers 400 or 413 if it wishes, and the connection then closes.

HttpConnection::respond fn

Writes a response with status, headers and body.

The status line carries reason_phrase(status). Content-Length and Connection among headers are dropped: Content-Length is written from body (not for 1xx, 204 or 304), and Connection as negotiated. The body is left out after a HEAD request and for a status that has none. After a response that ends the connection, the connection is closed and request gives None.

HttpConnection::close fn

Ends the connection: closes its sending side, or sends TLS's close_notify on an https connection.

Does nothing on a connection already closed.

std::database impl/std/database.cb

Scram struct

The client's side of one SCRAM-SHA-256 exchange (RFC 5802, RFC 7677), without channel binding.

The steps in order: Scram::start, send Scram::client_first, answer the server's first message with Scram::respond, then check the server's final message with Scram::verify. The PostgreSQL client uses it; it is exported so a program can speak the exchange to another server.

Scram::start fn

A new exchange for user with the client's nonce client_nonce.

, and = in user are escaped as =2C and =3D. The nonce should be fresh random text for each exchange, such as the base64 of bytes from os_random_bytes. PostgreSQL ignores the user, and its client sends "".

Scram::client_first fn

The client's first message, n,,n=USER,r=NONCE: no channel binding.

Scram::respond fn

The client's final message, carrying the proof of password, for the server's first message.

server_first is the server's r=…,s=…,i=…. Remembers the signature Scram::verify then expects. Err(AuthFailed) when the server's nonce does not begin with the client's and add to it; Err(ProtocolViolation) when the message is malformed, asks for an extension (m=), gives an iteration count of 0 or a salt that is not base64.

Scram::verify fn

Whether the server's final message (v=…) carries the signature this exchange expects.

false for anything else, an e= error among them, and false before Scram::respond has succeeded (there is no signature to expect yet).

scram_salted_password fn

The SCRAM-SHA-256 salted password: PBKDF2 over HMAC-SHA-256 of password and salt, 32 bytes.

iterations is the server's count. The password is used as given, with no SASLprep normalisation.

std::database::postgres impl/std/database/postgres.cb

PgError enum

Why a PostgreSQL connection or statement failed.

  • PgNetFailure(e): connecting, reading or writing failed; e says how.
  • PgTlsFailure(e): the TLS handshake or the encrypted stream failed.
  • TlsRefused: the server does not accept TLS, and the URL asks for verify-full.
  • NoTrustedRoots: the system's trusted roots could not be loaded.
  • BadConnectionUrl: the URL is malformed (PgUrl::parse).
  • UnsupportedAuth: the server asks for a method other than SCRAM-SHA-256 or a password over TLS.
  • AuthRefused: the server asks for the password in clear over an unencrypted connection.
  • AuthFailed: the server refused the credentials, or failed to prove it knows them.
  • Server(e): the server reported an error; the connection stays usable.
  • ProtocolViolation: a message from the server is malformed or not allowed at that point.
  • ResultTooLarge: the rows exceed max_result, or more than 65 535 parameters were given.
  • Disconnected: the stream ended, or the connection was closed or broken by an earlier failure.

PgError::text fn

e as text for a message; a server error as severity: message (code).

PgServerError struct

An error or notice the server reported.

severity is ERROR, FATAL, NOTICE and so on; code the five-character SQLSTATE; message the text; detail, hint and position (a character position from 1 into the statement) when the server gave them.

PgSslMode enum

Whether a connection is encrypted.

  • Disable: not encrypted.
  • VerifyFull: TLS, with the server's certificate verified for the host name against the trusted roots.

An unverified TLS connection is not offered.

PgUrl struct

A parsed connection URL, postgres://user[:password]@host[:port]/database[?sslmode=MODE].

user, password and database are percent-decoded; host is a name, an IPv4 literal or an IPv6 literal without its brackets.

PgUrl::parse fn

The connection URL text taken apart.

The scheme is postgres or postgresql. The port defaults to 5432, the database to the user, sslmode to verify-full; the only query key is sslmode, disable or verify-full. Err(BadConnectionUrl) for another scheme, no user, no host, a port that is not a number, another query key or mode, or a bad percent-encoding.

PgValue enum

A statement parameter, sent in the text form the server reads for it.

The server infers each parameter's type from the statement. PgValue::text gives the text each variant is sent as.

PgValue::text fn

The text value is sent as; None for Null.

An integer and a float as decimal text (a float that is not finite as Infinity, -Infinity or NaN), a bool as t or f, bytes as bytea's hex form (\x and the hex digits).

PgColumn struct

One column of a result: its name and the OID of its type (23 for int4, 25 for text, 16 for bool).

PgRow struct

One row of a result: a cell per column, NULL as None, every other value as the server's text form.

PgRow::get fn

The text of the cell at column i of r; None for NULL or past the last column.

PgRow::get_i64 fn

The cell at column i of r read as an i64.

None for NULL, past the last column, or for text that is not an integer; PgRow::get still gives the text.

PgRow::get_f64 fn

The cell at column i of r read as an f64, NaN, Infinity and -Infinity included.

None for NULL, past the last column, or for text that is not a number.

PgRow::get_bool fn

The cell at column i of r read as a bool: t is true, f is false.

None for NULL, past the last column, or for any other text.

PgRow::get_bytes fn

The cell at column i of r read as bytes from bytea's hex form (\x and hex digits).

None for NULL, past the last column, or for text of another form.

PgResult struct

What a statement gave: its columns and rows, the count of rows affected, and the command tag.

columns and rows are empty for a statement without a result set. affected is the number the tag ends with, 0 when it has none; tag is the tag itself (SELECT 3, INSERT 0 1, CREATE TABLE).

PgResult::column fn

The index of the first column named exactly name; None when there is none.

PgConnection struct

An open connection to a PostgreSQL server.

Not independently audited: this client is implemented to PostgreSQL's wire protocol and RFC 5802 and RFC 7677, tested against their vectors and against a PostgreSQL server on loopback, and fuzzed continuously; it has not been independently audited.

One statement runs at a time, its parameters bound (never spliced into the SQL text), and rows come back as text. A connection is one thread's: a program that queries from several threads keeps a connection per thread. notices holds the notices received so far, for the program to read and clear; max_result is the most a statement's rows may take in bytes (16 MiB). Dropping a connection without PgConnection::close closes the socket without telling the server. No binary rows, cursors, COPY, LISTEN/NOTIFY, cancellation or channel binding.

PgConnection::connect fn

Connects to the server url names, with a 30-second timeout and the system's trusted roots.

The roots are loaded only for verify-full: Err(NoTrustedRoots) when they cannot be. Otherwise as PgConnection::connect_with.

PgConnection::connect_with fn

Connects to the server url names, verifying its certificate against roots.

roots is unused for sslmode=disable. timeout_ms bounds connecting to each of the host's addresses in turn and then every read and write. Authenticates by SCRAM-SHA-256, or by the password over TLS only. Its errors include BadConnectionUrl, PgNetFailure when no address connects, TlsRefused, PgTlsFailure, UnsupportedAuth, AuthRefused, AuthFailed, Server and ProtocolViolation.

PgConnection::parameter fn

The value the server reported for the run-time parameter name at startup; None when it gave none.

Such as server_version, server_encoding or TimeZone.

PgConnection::query fn

Runs one statement with $1, $2, ... bound to params, and gives its result.

A server error is Err(Server(e)) once the server is ready again, and the connection stays usable; Err(ResultTooLarge) when the rows exceed max_result, also leaving it usable. A network or protocol failure closes the connection, and every later call gives Err(Disconnected). Transactions are statements: BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK.

PgConnection::execute fn

Runs a statement without rows, as PgConnection::query does, and gives the count of rows it affected.

PgConnection::run_script fn

Runs sql as a script of statements separated by ;, without parameters, discarding every result.

The first server error is Err(Server(e)). Not for COPY. Err(Disconnected) on a closed connection.

PgConnection::close fn

Tells the server the session is over and closes the connection; nothing when it is already closed.

std::encoding::json impl/std/encoding/json.cb

Json enum

A JSON value: null, a boolean, a number, a string, an array or an object.

  • JsonNull, JsonBool(b): null, true and false.
  • JsonNumber(x): every number is an f64, so an integer beyond 2^53 loses precision.
  • JsonText(s): a string, its escapes decoded.
  • JsonArray(items): the elements, in order.
  • JsonObject(members): the members in the order read or added; duplicate keys are kept as read.

The variant names carry Json so that none clashes with another std enum's. Dropping a Json frees the whole tree.

Json::parse fn

The JSON value text holds, with any white space around it.

  • Err(Empty) when the text holds no value at all.
  • Err(Invalid(i)) at the first byte that does not fit, or the length when the text stops short.
  • Err(OutOfRange) for a number beyond f64, or arrays and objects nested deeper than 512.

In a string, a surrogate pair written as two \u escapes is joined, and a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD.

Json::text fn

The value j as compact JSON text: no white space, members and elements in order.

A whole number within 2^53 is written without a fraction, any other in the shortest digits that read back as it, and a NaN or an infinity, which JSON cannot write, as null. Strings escape ", \ and the control characters; other characters, non-ASCII included, are written as they are. Apart from a NaN or an infinity, Json::parse of the text gives j back.

Json::pretty fn

The value j as JSON text for people: one element or member per line, two spaces per level.

A key is followed by : , an empty array or object stays [] or {}, and there is no newline at the end. Numbers and strings are written as Json::text writes them.

Json::get fn

The value of the first member named key when j is an object, else None.

None also when there is no such member.

Json::at fn

Element i of j when j is an array, else None.

None also when i is past the end.

Json::lookup fn

The value at the dotted path below j: Json::lookup(&doc, "servers.0.host").

Each part of the path names a member of an object, or, where the value reached is an array, an element by its index written in decimal. None when any part is not there. A key that itself contains a dot is reached with Json::get.

Json::is_null fn

Whether j is JsonNull.

Json::as_bool fn

The boolean j holds, or None when j is not JsonBool.

Json::as_f64 fn

The number j holds, or None when j is not JsonNumber.

Json::as_i64 fn

The number j holds as an integer, or None when it is not a number, not whole, or outside i64.

Json::as_text fn

A view of the string j holds, or None when j is not JsonText.

Json::as_array fn

The elements of j when it is an array, or None for another kind of value.

Json::as_object fn

The members of j, in order, when it is an object, or None for another kind of value.

Json::set fn

Sets member key of the object j to v.

The first member of that name is replaced, or else a new member appended. Faults (diag.assert-failed) when j is not an object.

Json::push fn

Appends v to the array j.

Faults (diag.assert-failed) when j is not an array.

JsonMember struct

One member of a JSON object: its key and its value.

  • key: the member's name, its escapes decoded.
  • value: its value.

std::encoding::hex impl/std/encoding/hex.cb

to_hex fn

The bytes as lowercase hexadecimal text, two digits each.

from_hex fn

The bytes the hexadecimal text spells, two digits a byte, in either case.

  • Err(Empty) for empty text (base64_decode gives no bytes instead).
  • Err(Invalid(i)) at the first byte that is not a hexadecimal digit.
  • Err(Invalid(len)) when the digits are odd in number.

std::encoding::base64 impl/std/encoding/base64.cb

base64_encode fn

The bytes in base64 (RFC 4648 §4), padded with = to a multiple of four characters.

The alphabet is the standard one: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, + and /.

base64_decode fn

The bytes the base64 text spells, read as base64_encode writes it.

Padding is required. Empty text gives no bytes.

  • Err(Invalid(len)) when the length is not a multiple of four.
  • Err(Invalid(i)) at the first byte that is not a base64 character; a = before the final one or two is such a byte.
  • Err(Invalid(i)) at the last character before the padding when it leaves bits over that are not zero: "QR==" is refused, since base64_encode writes "A" as "QQ==". Each byte string has one text.

std::encoding::toml impl/std/encoding/toml.cb

Toml enum

A TOML value: a string, an integer, a float, a boolean, a date-time, an array or a table.

  • TomlString(s): a string, its escapes decoded.
  • TomlInteger(i): an integer, exact in i64.
  • TomlFloat(x): a float, inf and nan included.
  • TomlBool(b): true or false.
  • TomlDateTime(d): one of the four date-time forms (see TomlDateTime).
  • TomlArray(items): the elements, in order; elements may be of different kinds.
  • TomlTable(members): the members in the order read or added; a key occurs once.

The variant names carry Toml so that none clashes with another std enum's. Dropping a Toml frees the whole tree.

Toml::parse fn

The TOML document text holds, as a table.

The whole of TOML 1.0: tables and arrays of tables under headers, dotted keys, inline tables, the four string forms with every escape, integers in decimal, hexadecimal, octal and binary with underscores, floats with inf and nan, and the four date-time forms. An empty document is an empty table.

  • Err(Invalid(i)) at the first byte that does not fit, or at a key that is defined twice or would add to a table the format has closed (one defined by an earlier header, or an inline table).
  • Err(OutOfRange) for an integer beyond i64, a float beyond f64, or arrays and inline tables nested deeper than 512.

Err(Empty) never occurs: a document with no key is an empty table.

Toml::text fn

The value t as TOML text.

A table is written as a document: its plain members as key = value lines, then each member that is a table under a [header], and each non-empty array of tables under [[headers]], in order, recursively; a key is bare when it can be and quoted otherwise. Strings are basic strings with ", \ and the control characters escaped; a float is written in the shortest digits that read back as it, with inf and nan; a date-time as TomlDateTime::text writes it. A value that is not a table is written in the form it takes after =: arrays as [a, b], inline tables as { k = v }. Comments are not kept. Toml::parse of the text gives t back, the plain members of each table before its sub-tables.

Toml::get fn

The value of the member named key when t is a table, else None.

None also when there is no such member.

Toml::at fn

Element i of t when t is an array, else None.

None also when i is past the end.

Toml::lookup fn

The value at the dotted path below t: Toml::lookup(&doc, "database.ports.0").

Each part of the path names a member of a table, or, where the value reached is an array, an element by its index written in decimal. None when any part is not there. A key that itself contains a dot is reached with Toml::get.

Toml::as_text fn

The string t holds as a view, or None when t is not TomlString.

Toml::as_i64 fn

The integer t holds, or None when t is not TomlInteger.

Toml::as_f64 fn

The float t holds, or None when t is not TomlFloat; an integer is not converted.

Toml::as_bool fn

The boolean t holds, or None when t is not TomlBool.

Toml::as_datetime fn

The date-time t holds, or None when t is not TomlDateTime.

Toml::as_array fn

The elements of t when it is an array, or None for another kind of value.

Toml::as_table fn

The members of t, in order, when it is a table, or None for another kind of value.

Toml::set fn

Sets member key of the table t to v.

The member of that name is replaced, or else a new member appended. Faults (diag.assert-failed) when t is not a table.

Toml::push fn

Appends v to the array t.

Faults (diag.assert-failed) when t is not an array.

TomlMember struct

One member of a TOML table: its key and its value.

  • key: the member's name, one key part (a dotted key a.b is a member a holding a table with a member b).
  • value: its value.

TomlDateKind enum

Which of the four date-time forms a TomlDateTime is.

  • TomlOffsetDateTime: a date, a time and an offset from UTC: 1979-05-27T07:32:00Z, …-08:00.
  • TomlLocalDateTime: a date and a time with no offset: 1979-05-27T07:32:00.
  • TomlLocalDate: a date alone: 1979-05-27.
  • TomlLocalTime: a time alone: 07:32:00.

TomlDateTime struct

A TOML date-time: the fields of RFC 3339's form, and kind, which of the four forms it is.

  • kind: the form; the fields a form does not have are 0.
  • year, month, day: the date (month 1 to 12, day 1 to the month's length).
  • hour, minute, second: the time (second up to 60 for a leap second).
  • nanoseconds: the fraction of the second, 0 to 999 999 999; digits beyond nine are dropped when read.
  • offset_minutes: the offset from UTC in minutes, -1439 to 1439; 0 for every other form.

A plain struct, assigned by copying. TomlDateTime::text writes it as the format does.

TomlDateTime::text fn

The date-time as TOML (and RFC 3339) writes it: the date, T, the time, its fraction when there is one, and the offset as Z or ±HH:MM; a local form leaves out what it does not have.

std::compress impl/std/compress.cb

CompressError enum

Why a stream could not be decompressed.

  • Corrupt(i): the stream is not DEFLATE (or not the wrapper asked for), or its checksum does not match, first seen at byte i.
  • Truncated: the stream ends before its last block or its trailer.
  • Oversize: the output would exceed the max given.

CompressError::text fn

A short description of e for a message, such as corrupt compressed data.

inflate fn

The bytes a raw DEFLATE stream (RFC 1951, no header or checksum) encodes, at most max of them.

Err(Oversize) as soon as the output would exceed max: a limit against a small stream that expands without bound. Err(Truncated) when data ends inside a block; Err(Corrupt(i)) at byte i for a malformed block. Bytes after the final block are ignored. Reads stored, fixed and dynamic Huffman blocks.

deflate fn

data compressed as a raw DEFLATE stream (RFC 1951, no header or checksum).

One fixed strategy, so every implementation writes the same bytes: LZ77 over a 32 KiB window, each block stored, fixed or dynamic Huffman, whichever is shortest. Empty data is one empty block (03 00).

adler32 fn

The Adler-32 checksum of data (RFC 1950), zlib's checksum; 1 for no bytes.

For CRC-32, gzip's checksum, use crc32 in std::crypto.

zlib_deflate fn

data compressed as a zlib stream (RFC 1950): a two-byte header, the DEFLATE stream, the Adler-32.

zlib_inflate fn

The bytes a zlib stream encodes, at most max of them, its header checked and its checksum verified.

Err(Corrupt(0)) for a header that is not DEFLATE without a preset dictionary; Err(Corrupt(i)) at the trailer when the Adler-32 does not match; Err(Truncated) for fewer than 6 bytes or a missing trailer; otherwise as inflate, Err(Oversize) included.

gzip fn

data compressed as a gzip file (RFC 1952), with no name, time or extra fields in its header.

The trailer holds the CRC-32 and the length of data modulo 2 to the power 32.

gunzip fn

The bytes a gzip file encodes, every member in turn, at most max of them.

Each header's optional fields are skipped. Err(Corrupt(i)) at a header that is not gzip's, or at a trailer whose CRC-32 or length does not match; Err(Truncated) for a member cut short; otherwise as inflate, Err(Oversize) included.

std::ffi impl/std/ffi.cb

NulError struct

The error of text that holds a NUL byte, which C would take as its end.

offset is the position of the first NUL.

NulError::text fn

A short description of the error for messages: "holds a NUL byte".

CString struct

Text followed by one NUL byte, for a C function that takes const char *.

Made by CString::new or CString::from_bytes, which refuse text that already holds a NUL. CString::ptr is the address to pass; it stays valid while the CString lives, even if the CString itself is moved, and dropping the CString frees the bytes. The C function must not write through the address or keep it.

CString::from_bytes fn

b with a NUL byte after it, or Err with the position of the first NUL already in b.

The bytes need not be UTF-8: a path or a name from another system is often not.

CString::new fn

s with a NUL byte after it, or Err with the position of the first NUL already in s.

A literal where a StringView is expected is made into one: CString::new("HOME").

CString::ptr fn

The address of the first byte, to pass to C as a const char *.

Taking the address is safe; the call that uses it is inside unsafe. The address is valid until the CString is dropped.

CString::len fn

The length of the text, without the NUL.

CString::as_bytes fn

The text without the NUL, as bytes.

copy_to_raw fn

The elements of s, plain data, copied to C memory at p: an output buffer a C caller owns (D-0257). Called inside unsafe { } ([Trusted-Call]): the caller vouches that p has room for them and that nothing else uses that memory for the call.

is_null fn

Whether p is C's NULL, the address null_rawptr<T>().

C functions return NULL for "none": getenv of a name that is not set, fopen of a file that cannot be opened. Testing for it is safe; reading through p is not.
